correctness.rationale: The graph vertices are exactly 112 labeled three-subsets, 10-regular with 560 edges. A 56-element affine orbit lists every triple exactly once, and the displayed 10-cycle lists the entire connection set. The specified two cyclic rotations produce a bijective dart face-permutation whose all 1120 darts are partitioned into 280 distinct simple 4-faces. A separate field/group check exhaustively confirms both product and closure identities for every one of the 10 local connection labels. The ribbon-graph rotation system defines a connected orientable cellular embedding of genus 85. Existence of 4-cycle faces makes the graph bridgeless; bipartite face lengths >=4 then give genus >= 1-V/2+E/4=85. The finite checking is exhaustive for this one graph, not an extrapolation to a family; two code paths run from actual included sources.

value.rationale: The paper that first publicly motivates the question lists a substantial unresolved genus interval 85–143 for this exact smallest exceptional k=3 bipartite Kneser graph. The certificate closes that finite invariant completely and realizes its lower Euler bound with a highly symmetric map, giving a reusable explicit rotation witness for the previously inaccessible 3-subset case. This is neither a degree-only bound nor a routine instance of the published k=2 theorem. The result has independent value as a natural exact genus determination, without claiming a general family theorem.
